curriculum.subject: English Language Activities
curriculum.outcomeText: appreciate the importance of using singular and plural nouns correctly in communication.

interactions.prompt: You see one cup. Which words tell it clearly?
interactions.feedback: Yes! One cup names a single thing clearly.
interactions.retryHint: One means there is only a single cup.

interactions.prompt: You see three books. Complete: I see three ___.
interactions.feedback: Great! We add -s to book when there is more than one.
interactions.retryHint: More than one book needs the plural ending -s.

interactions.prompt: Match each amount to the clear noun phrase.
interactions.tapAlternative: Tap an amount, then tap its matching words.
interactions.feedback: Well done! Your nouns tell exactly how many.
interactions.retryHint: Use no plural ending for one; use -s or -es for many.

interactions.prompt: Musa asks for two brushes. Which sentence is clear?
interactions.feedback: Correct! Two brushes uses the plural noun correctly.
interactions.retryHint: The number two must be followed by a word meaning many.

interactions.prompt: Sort the phrases into clear or needs-fixing.
interactions.tapAlternative: Tap a phrase, then choose clear or needs-fixing.
interactions.feedback: Excellent! Correct singulars and plurals prevent mix-ups.
interactions.retryHint: Check whether the number is one or many, then check the noun ending.

interactions.prompt: Your teacher needs five boxes. Which message gives the right information?
interactions.feedback: Fantastic! The correct plural makes your message clear.
interactions.retryHint: Five means many, and box takes -es when it means many.
